title: Spline jitter: tiling vs tilt bench notes
content:
Summary:
This is a lightweight lab notebook comparing two slot-allocation heuristics we prototyped: tiling (baseline tiling scheduler) vs. tilt (a new 'tilt' heuristic that biases slot assignment to reduce slot-switch jitter at the cost of slightly higher idle fill). Goal: measure p50/p90/p99 latency, observed jitter (micro-slew across seconds), and cost-per-1k-requests (approx dollars estimate using our cluster unit pricing).

High-level takeaways (quick):
- Tilt reduced p99 by ~8-12% on sparse conversational workloads (sessionized burst mix) compared to tiling, but increased average GPU idle by ~3.5 percentage points (cost delta).
- For dense steady-state batches (high concurrency long contexts) tiling remains slightly cheaper (~2-4% lower dollar/1k) with no meaningful latency regression.
- Tilt shines when session churn is high (many short sessions with interleaved turns) — jitter waveform amplitude collapses, improving tail.
- Action: run a 2-week A/B (small % traffic) on a hosted route with conversation-turn profile before merging into default pacing knob set.

Experimental setup:
- Cluster: dev-cluster-tiltlab, 8x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes, standard runtime kernels.
- Runtime build: branch feat/tilt-proto (PR link above), optimization flags identical to baseline.
- Client workload generator: local harness (synth-turn-gen v0.9.2), replayed traces from prod-sampled session set (2029-04) with two profiles:
  * Profile A: conversational micro (90% sessions < 3 turns, median inter-turn 15s, peaks at 400 rps)
  * Profile B: long-context steady (50% sessions > 30 turns, sustained 1k concurrency)
- Measurement window: 60m steady run, repeated 6 times, discard first 5m warmup.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), jitter (per-second p90 delta), GPU duty-cycle (busy%), slot-fill efficiency, estimated $/1k requests (using internal unit cost 0.00032 $/gpu-second baseline).
- Notes: we intentionally left KV-cache warmup identical; tilt only changes slot dooring and preemption biasing.

Raw-ish results (median across runs) — ascii sparklines and mini-tables: 

Profile A (conversational micro) — latency percentiles (ms):
  tiling : p50=21   p90=78   p99=312
  tilt   : p50=22   p90=69   p99=274

p99 delta: tilt vs tiling = -38ms (~-12.2%)

Jitter waveform (per-second p90 delta, bigger is worse):
  tiling : ████▇▅▃▂ (avg amplitude ~48ms)
  tilt   : ██▇▅▃▁  (avg amplitude ~17ms)

GPU duty & cost:
  tiling : busy=74.1%  idle=25.9%  est $/1k = $0.94
  tilt   : busy=70.6%  idle=29.4%  est $/1k = $0.98

Interpretation: tilt trades 4-ish percentage points of duty-cycle for lower jitter and tail latency on sparse session workloads. Net cost increase ~4.3% but p99 improves ~12% — good trade when SLOs weight tail heavily.

Profile B (long-context steady) — latency percentiles (ms):
  tiling : p50=28   p90=95   p99=205
  tilt   : p50=27   p90=97   p99=212

p99 delta: tilt vs tiling = +7ms (~+3.4%)

GPU duty & cost:
  tiling : busy=88.9%  idle=11.1%  est $/1k = $0.73
  tilt   : busy=86.3%  idle=13.7%  est $/1k = $0.76

Interpretation: in dense steady workloads tilt slightly increases tail and reduces efficiency. Tiling remains preferable when throughput efficiency is primary.

Micro-observations & traces:
- We saw sequences where tiling causes slot shuffling across sessions at ~300ms cadence leading to amplified p99 during short spikes. Tilt reduces preemption frequency for recently-active sessions which preserves their soft-affinity and avoids repeated context reloads.
- Tilt introduces a small compaction effect: more idle slots because the scheduler holds onto slots longer (bias window = 450ms default). We profiled that bias window and saw diminishing returns after ~700ms (no extra latency benefit, more idle cost).
- Under network jitter (client side 50–200ms added), tilt maintained p99 advantage; suggests benefit is intra-node scheduler noise reduction rather than external network ordering.

ASCII cost/latency canvas (simplified cost vs p99):
  Profile A:  (x axis = est $/1k, lower is left)
    [tiling]  $0.94 |----------------------------- p99 312ms
    [tilt]    $0.98 |---------------------- p99 274ms
  Profile B:
    [tiling]  $0.73 |------------------ p99 205ms
    [tilt]    $0.76 |------------------- p99 212ms

Parameter sweep notes (short):
- Bias window (tilt.hold_ms): tested [100, 250, 450, 700, 1200] — knee at 450–700ms. Recommend default 450ms for conversational routes.
- Preempt aggression (tilt.preempt_thresh): higher values reduce idle but reintroduce jitter. Recommend exposing as a per-route knob in console (dev UX item).
- Combine tilt + lightweight tile-tiling (hybrid): we tried a hybrid where tilt active during low fill (<75% duty) and tiling otherwise — this got ~80% of tilt tail benefit with only ~1.5% duty penalty. Promising for autoswitch.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run a small % production A/B on 2 hosted routes (chat-widget-short-turns and assistant-qa-long) for 14 days to capture real traffic shape variance.
- Add more realistic client mix with mobile-handshake latencies and real upstream retries (we stripped retries in this run).
- Cost model needs incorporate pre-warm amortization for sessions resumed from cold (we did not include long-term session stickiness).

Action items (owner):
- (Aisha) prepare traffic-slice gating checklist + rollout playbook (ETA: 2029-05-24).
- (Carlos) instrument tilt.bias-window telemetry to show per-tenant duty delta (ETA: 2029-05-22).
- (Evelyn) prototype hybrid autoswitch rule in the simulator and run 24h sweep (ETA: 2029-05-28).

Appendix — short reproducibility notes:
- Docker image: redwood/runtime:tilt-proto-20290515
- Trace bundle: s3://redwood-sampled-traces/prod/2029-04/conv-micro-v1.tar.gz
- Exact command used: runbench --profile conv-micro --clients 200 --duration 3600 --warmup 300 --scheduler [tiling|tilt] --seed 20290517

Quick log excerpt (tilt run) — illustrative: 
  [2029-05-17T13:23:02Z] scheduler: tilt assigned slot S=0x7f9 to session sid=8823 hold_ms=450
  [2029-05-17T13:23:02Z] session: sid=8823 turn=2 latency=48ms (p99 window)
  [2029-05-17T13:23:02Z] scheduler: preempt consider sid=9130 idle_since=210ms -> skipped (tilt bias)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally concise — meant to be a lab-first artifact to collect feedback. If we agree tilt merits rollout, follow-ups: formalize tuning matrix, update console route knobs, and add billing projections for mixed-tilt rollout (customer tier specific).

Links/refs: JIRA-ENG-1428 (tilt prototype epic), GH PR above, internal billing doc: confluence/redwood/cost-models#2029-tilt-sweep

End of notes.
